title: Azure Monitor — Simply Explained
description:
Jumping between five screens whenever something breaks? This episode explains Azure Monitor in plain English for Azure beginners and admins, covering metrics, logs, KQL, workbooks, alerts and the 2026 changes, plus practical tips to keep monitoring costs under control.
In this episode
00:00 – Too many dashboards00:35 – What is Azure Monitor?01:48 – Metrics and logs03:19 – Where the data comes from05:19 – Visualization: workbooks and dashboards07:07 – Alerts and automation09:13 – What's new in 202610:42 – Cost optimization and how it all fits together
Key takeaways
Azure Monitor is Microsoft's central observability platform: metrics tell you something is wrong, logs in a Log Analytics workspace queried with KQL tell you why.Data flows in from Azure resources, Application Insights, the Azure Monitor Agent (also via Azure Arc), Entra ID and security tools, and is visualized in workbooks and acted on with alerts, action groups and Logic Apps.Migrate off the retired Log Analytics agent, adopt OpenTelemetry, and control cost by tiering logs, setting per-table retention and using sampling and budget alerts.
Worth quoting
“Azure Monitor isn't a single tool. It's a platform that pulls together metrics, logs, traces, and alerts from Azure on premises and even other clouds.” – Mirko Peters (01:07)
“Metrics tell you something is wrong, logs tell you why. Imagine driving your car. The check engine light comes on, and that's a metric telling you something is wrong right now” – Mirko Peters (02:35)
Explore more on M365.FM
Episode page: the full episode with chapters, quotes and a short FAQ on Azure MonitorKusto Query Language (KQL) – the query language used to search logs in a Log Analytics workspace and write log alertsMicrosoft Entra ID – streams sign-in and audit logs into Azure Monitor and now secures Application Insights queriesAzure Logic Apps – triggered by action groups for automated remediation, such as running a disk cleanup scriptPower BI – the option for sharing monitoring reports with stakeholders who don't work in AzureRelated episode: Log Analytics - Simply Explained
